title: Common financial scams
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers the scam versus identity theft distinction and warning signs, but it does not teach the common scam types in the brief (fake shops, fake prizes, quick riches) or the social media targeting, and its focus on identity theft is a different idea.

draft.title: Common financial scams
card: A scam is a trick to take money or personal details from people. Scammers often pretend to be a real business, bank or person.
a message that pretends to be from a trusted company and asks for passwords or card details, often with a link to a fake website.
a website or social media page that takes payment for goods that never arrive, or sends poor copies.
a message saying you won something you never entered, or an offer of fast, easy money. Young people are often targeted on social media.
draft.remember: Scams come in many forms, but each one tries to get your money or your details.

a.q: Zara gets a text saying it is from her bank. It asks her to tap a link and type in her password. What type of scam is this?
a.why: Phishing pretends to be a trusted company to get passwords or card details. It is not a fake shop, because nothing is being sold, and it does not promise a prize or easy money.
a.clue: Who is the message pretending to be, and what does it want?

b.q: Leo sees a social media page selling cheap football boots. He pays, but nothing ever arrives and the page disappears. Which scam is this?
b.why: Leo paid for goods that never came, which is a fake online shop. It is tempting to call it phishing, but the page did not ask for his passwords by pretending to be a trusted company.
b.clue: What did Leo pay for, and what did he get?
